title: Create the normalized ground-truth annotation provider
evidence_required: Ground-Truth Annotations Calculation-Ready Owner Boundary RED: the current diagnostics persistence rejects participant_name/annotations in ordinary evidence and exposes no normalized annotation table or calculation projection; GREEN: a next-linear migration and diagnostics-owned provider persist only valid detection correct|false or person missed rows, reject invalid/nonexistent targets, support correction/removal and return only explicit immutable rows while absence contributes nothing; decisive comparison: disposable migration plus repository/application fixtures across valid, invalid, absent and explicit-missed cases with unchanged promo-owned rows; artifact: redacted provider evidence under .tasks/TASK-096-T3-FT-010-W1/.
purpose: Provide the smallest protected diagnostics-owned persistence and application boundary that later HTML and Calibration flows can reuse without putting names in ordinary evidence or inventing participant identity state.
success_outcome: Diagnostics persists only valid normalized annotation rows for existing Attempts and exposes an immutable calculation snapshot in which absent ground truth is excluded and person-level missed needs no detector artifact.
anti_goals: Do not add the staff HTML flow, Calibration calculations, promotion/retention integration or production configuration.
Do not add a participant registry, identity clustering, dataset/history table, JSON payload column, frame upload or detector-miss proof.
Do not put participant names or annotations in ordinary_manifest, structured server events, URLs or retained unredacted task artifacts.

forbidden_scope: Production PostgreSQL, operator/default Attempts/evidence and real participant names
Promo Attempt/result/session mutation, cross-owner foreign keys/cascades and direct foreign-table writes
Staff annotation routes, Calibration algorithms/runs, retention cleanup and promoted-subset behavior
stop_conditions: Calculation-ready semantics cannot remain a diagnostics-owned normalized table plus immutable application projection.
A valid person-level missed annotation would require a detector occurrence, reference-frame upload or participant registry.
The migration cannot remain next-linear in the one shared schema/Base/Alembic stream without a cross-owner cascade.
T3 protected-data probes cannot use synthetic names, disposable rows, safe rerun, redacted artifacts and complete cleanup.

constraints: Primary owner is diagnostics at src/face_moment/diagnostics/; promo supplies immutable Attempt truth only through its accepted query boundary.
Create one next-linear migration from the execution-time direct predecessor; prove only this revision's upgrade/downgrade and linear ancestry on a disposable task database.
Persist only annotation_id, attempt_id, target kind/index, bounded participant_name and outcome; add no audit/history, participant or dataset model.
Detection correct|false requires a current evidence occurrence; person missed has no occurrence and no mandatory artifact, but expired/removed ordinary state rejects every new write.
Use a partial uniqueness rule only for one detection target per Attempt; multiple person-level missed rows remain valid.
Retain only synthetic names/UUIDs and redacted evidence; cleanup cannot touch operator/default state.
invariants: Diagnostics is the only writer of annotation state and never mutates promo Attempts/results/sessions.
Participant names and annotations never enter ordinary_manifest or structured server events.
No annotation row means no calculation outcome; explicit missed is persisted only as a person-level row.
The single PostgreSQL schema/Base/Alembic stream remains linear and has no ownership-crossing cascade.
verification_targets: Disposable PostgreSQL migration/repository fixtures prove exact checks, detection-target uniqueness, no cross-owner FK/cascade, valid create/correct/remove/list and persistence across a new session.

Application fixtures distinguish absent annotation from explicit person-level missed and reject nonexistent detection targets plus expired/removed writes without requiring frame upload or detector-miss evidence.
Ownership/import and SQL inspection prove diagnostics-only writes through accepted promo reads, unchanged promo rows and no participant/history/dataset/JSON-bundle model.
